inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL aggregation lesson demonstrates ordered GROUP_CONCAT for grouped names and JSON_OBJECTAGG for key/value totals as adjacent reporting patterns.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as one team activity report that combines ordered distinct member-name concatenation, JSON_OBJECTAGG project-hour mappings, and numeric totals per team. The source tables, identifiers, values, course framing, and separate example queries are not copied.

fixture_notes: Red has Ava on two projects and Bo on one, so DISTINCT GROUP_CONCAT returns Ava and Bo once each while JSON_OBJECTAGG retains one entry per project. Blue has Dee and Eli on separate projects; all rows are active.
determinism_notes: Fixed activity IDs, explicit derived-input ordering, member-name ordering inside GROUP_CONCAT, unique project keys per team, stable team ordering, and no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE team_activity (activity_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, member_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, project_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, hours INT NOT NULL, active TINYINT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT team_code, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT member_name ORDER BY member_name SEPARATOR '|') AS member_names, JSON_OBJECTAGG(project_code, hours) AS project_hours, SUM(hours) AS total_hours FROM (SELECT activity_id, team_code, member_name, project_code, hours FROM team_activity WHERE active = 1 ORDER BY team_code, activity_id) AS ordered_activity GROUP BY team_code ORDER BY team_code

checks.sql: SELECT activity_id, team_code, member_name, project_code, hours, active FROM team_activity ORDER BY activity_id
